newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA attacks high charges faced by airlines.
newsitem.headline: IATA attacks high charges faced by airlines.

text.p: Airlines must fight unfair price fixing policies set by monopolies providing many of the services needed by airlines and their "inflated charges which we ultimately have to pass on to our passengers," Swissair and IATA president, Otto Loepfe said on Monday.
"All our airlines have one thing in common: we aren't making enough money," he told the International Air Transport Association's annual general meeting
Although some of the reasons for this relate to the airlines themselves and to their markets, "a number of our problems can also be attributed to the regulatory environment we work in."
"And many of these can be ascribed to one major cause: the monopolies enjoyed by many of the providers of the services we need," he added.

"From their privileged position, and often encouraged by the states they serve, they charge fees for their services that hit and hurt all of us so much that they seriously threaten our chances of long-term survival," Loepfe said.

It called upon "the relevant authorities to implement an independent regulatory process for approving charges, setting economic performances targets and protecting airlines and their passengers from monopoly abuse."

Airlines are "powerless to oppose luxuries an airport decides we should have, powerless to object to expensive and incompatible ATC systems acquired primarily for reasons of national prestige and powerless to protest when we are used as a convenient cash cow to reduce local budgeting shortfalls that have nothing to do with us or our activities."Loepfe added.
